He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== Bagley attended [[Corona del Sol High School]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]] as a freshman and Hillcrest Prep in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] as a sophomore.{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/08/17/marvin-bagley-iii-leaving-corona-del-sol-join-hillcrest-hoops/31892649/|title=Marvin Bagley III leaving Corona del Sol to join Hillcrest Hoops|publisher=}} During that sophomore year, he was teammates with [[Deandre Ayton]]. In 2016, he transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14487033/no-1-sophomore-marvin-bagley-iii-enrolls-sierra-canyon-school-california|title=No. 1 sophomore Bagley enrolls at Sierra Canyon|publisher=}}{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/01/27/marvin-bagley-iii-awaits-appeal-decision-cites-academics-transfer-reason/79400164/|title=Marvin Bagley III awaits appeal decision, cites academics as transfer reason|publisher=}} He was ruled ineligible to play his first year at Sierra Canyon due to [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) rules.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/14612607/marvin-bagley-iii-no-1-2018-class-ineligible-year|title=Bagley, No. 1 in 2018 class, ineligible this year|publisher=}}{{cite web|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20161205/sierra-canyons-marvin-bagley-iii-ready-to-make-impact-on-basketball-landscape|title=Sierra Canyon’s Marvin Bagley III ready to make impact on basketball landscape|date=6 December 2016|publisher=}} That ruling would help play a factor into reclassifying his senior year of high school up a year early. In his last season for Sierra Canyon, he averaged 24.9 [[points per game]] and 10.1 [[rebounds per game]]. He would be named for the All-[[USA Today]] First-team in 2017. Bagley is rated as a five-star recruit and was formerly ranked as the top player in the 2018 class before his reclassification.{{cite [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].{{cite web|url=http://abcnews.go.com/Sports/marvin-bagley-makes-duke-team-beat/story?id=49219675|title=Marvin Bagley makes Duke the team to beat -- again|first=A. B. C.|last=News|date=15 August 2017|website=ABC News}} While he is still a member of the Class of 2018 for Sierra Canyon, he filed for reclassification, which made him eligible for NCAA play.{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/8/14/16014732/marvin-bagley-iii-recruiting-duke-2018-nba-draft|title=No. 1 recruit Marvin Bagley III commits to Duke, plans to reclassify to play college ball next season|publisher=}} He graduated from Sierra Canyon on September 1, 2017 and made his way onto Duke's campus after finishing up his high school academics a week later.{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/marvin-bagley-iii-set-to-decide-on-reclass-and-college-tonight-duke-usc-ucla-arizona|title=Marvin Bagley III set to announce college and reclassification plans Monday|date=14 August 2017|publisher=}}{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marvin-bagley-iii-cleared-by-ncaa-will-play-for-duke-this-season/|title=Marvin Bagley III cleared by NCAA, will play for Duke this season|publisher=}} Bagley would make his Duke debut on November 10, 2017, recording 25 points and 10 rebounds in a win over [[Elon University]]. On November 24, Bagley recorded 34 points and a freshman record 15 rebounds for Duke as they defeated the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] 85–78 in overtime. He tied the freshman record in rebounds recorded 4 days later in their next game and scored 30 points in an 87–84 win over the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. It would be the first time a Duke player would record such numbers for the team since the 1960s. On December 30, Bagley recorded 32 points and a record-high 21 rebounds in a 100–93 win over the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. With the 30 points and 11 rebounds Bagley III recorded on a 89–71 win over the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] on January 13, 2018, he became the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]]'s newest record holder for most 30 point, 10 rebound double-doubles for a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.dukebasketballreport.com/2018/1/14/16889588/dukes-bagley-is-stalking-greatness-acc-basketball|title=Duke’s Bagley Is Stalking Greatness|publisher=}} At the end of the regular season, Bagley was named both the ACC's Rookie of the Year and Player of the Year, as well as become a member of the All-ACC first team.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22645651/duke-marvin-bagley-iii-uva-tony-bennett-earn-top-awards-acc|title=Duke's Bagley is ACC rookie, player of year|publisher=}} He was also named a consensus member of the All-American First-Team throughout multiple organizations. In addition to that, Bagley joined [[DeAndre Ayton]] and [[Trae Young]] to record the most freshmen players to join the consensus All-American First-Team in a season. Following Duke's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Bagley announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a lottery selection.{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22946809/duke-blue-devils-freshman-marvin-bagley-iii-declares-draft|title=Freshman Marvin Bagley III leaving Duke for NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=March 28, 2018}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] | 33 || 32 || 33.8 || .614 || .397 || .627 || 11.1 || 1.5 || .8 || .9 || 21.0 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Marvin has two younger brothers: Marcus (currently a high school sophomore) and 7-year-old Martay.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/07/31/marvin-bagley-reclassify|title=Marvin Bagley III's presence will have fast impact|publisher=}} His father, Marvin Jr., previously played college football at [[North Carolina A&T]], as well as with the [[Arizona Rattlers]] professionally. His father met his wife, Tracy Caldwell, while Marvin Jr. was playing with the Rattlers in the [[Arena Football League]]. Marvin Jr. currently coaches AAU basketball for the Nike Phamily.https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2018/5/27/17400062/james-hampton-nike-eybl-circuit-rip Bagley's younger brother, Marcus Bagley, has received offers from [[Arizona University|Arizona]], [[Arizona State University|Arizona State]], and [[UCLA]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Recruitment/Marcus-Bagley-97119/RecruitInterests|title=Marcus Bagley Recruit Interests|website=247sports.com}} While living in the Los Angeles area, Marvin volunteered at Hoops with Heart, a non-profit organization in the city that benefits underprivileged youth.{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211661562|title=Marvin Bagley III Bio|publisher=}} Marvin is the grandson of basketball player Jumpin' [[Joe Caldwell]].{{Cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2528633-meet-marvin-bagley-iii-the-coveted-recruit-with-unique-game-and-pedigree|title=Meet Marvin Bagley III, the Coveted Recruit with Unique Game and Pedigree|website=bleacherreport.com|access-date=2018-03-25}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211661562&DB_OEM_ID=4200 Duke Blue Devils bio] {{2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Pete Newell Big Man Award}} {{Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bagley, Marvin III}} [[Category:1999 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Arizona]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Tempe, Arizona]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]]
